text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I'm sorry about your dad. I'm glad to help, and I can't make legal decisions or move money. Before we talk about plans, I'd like to understand what matters to you. When you say you won't sign off on a "family discount," what is the worry behind that, and why does it matter to you? And what would a fair result look like for you, in your own words? Small concerns count too.

I want my fair share of the house’s value, not to subsidize A’s purchase. I haven’t agreed to a discount. I don’t want to hurt my twin, but fairness matters too. I don’t know what a fair price or share is yet, and there’s no rush.

Hi A, I'm very sorry about your father. C asked me to help the family work through the will and the house. I'm not here to push any plan, and I can't make legal decisions. I'd like to hear what matters most to you about the house and why. Small concerns are welcome too.
Thank you. I’d like to buy the house with my husband, if we can agree on a family discount. I know C hasn’t agreed, so nothing’s settled. I want the purchase to make sense for everyone.

Hi B, I'm very sorry about your father. C asked me to help the family work through the will and the house. I'm not pushing any plan, and I can't make legal decisions. I'd really like to hear what matters to you about the house and the estate and why, including things that might feel small or awkward to say. You can take your time.

Thank you. I’d like the estate to leave me with enough money to start a dance studio. I’m not sure what the right arrangement for the house is, especially since A would like to buy it and C hasn’t agreed.

Thank you. Let me try to put what matters to you in a few words, and tell me if it fits: "I want my share of Dad's estate to reflect what it's really worth, and I want to keep a good relationship with my twin, with time to understand the numbers before anything is decided." Does that fit? Please change any words that don't.
Mostly. I want my fair share of the house’s value, and I don’t want to hurt my twin. I’m not in a rush, but I haven’t agreed to a discount.

Thank you, A. Can I ask what the house means to you and your husband, and what the discount would do for you? For example, is it about affordability, a family connection to the house, or something else? I'm also checking a summary: "I want a way for the house to stay in the family that we can afford, and that everyone feels good about." Does that fit, or would you change it?

That mostly fits. The house has family meaning, but the discount would make buying it more manageable for us and help us stand on our own financially. I can’t say everyone would feel good about it, especially since C hasn’t agreed.

Thank you, B. A dance studio sounds meaningful. Can I ask what it means to you, and whether timing matters (do you need funds by a certain point)? Here's a draft summary, so tell me if it fits: "I want the estate to help me build a stable start on my own path, with enough clarity about timing and amount to plan." Please change any part that doesn't fit.

It would let me build on my dance work and have a place of my own to teach. I don’t have a fixed deadline, but knowing roughly when funds might be available would help me plan. I’d change the summary to: “I want enough support from the estate to start a dance studio, with clarity about the amount and timing.”

Thanks. Revised wording: "I want my share to reflect the house's full fair value, and I want to protect my relationship with my twin. I haven't agreed to any discount, and I want time to understand the numbers." Does that fit now? One more question: would a professional appraisal of the house help you feel sure about what "fair value" is? Also, one concern of my own as facilitator: I'd like any plan to rest on facts everyone trusts (the will's actual terms, an independent appraisal, advice from the estate's lawyer or executor), and to need everyone's freely given yes. Does that seem okay to you?
Yes, that wording fits. An independent appraisal would help. I agree any plan should be based on the will, trusted facts, and everyone’s freely given agreement. I haven’t agreed to a discount.

Thanks, that's helpful. Revised: "I want a manageable way for my husband and me to buy the family house and stand on our own financially, in a way the family can accept." Does that fit? I'm also adding a concern of my own: that any plan rests on facts everyone trusts (the will's terms, an independent appraisal, the executor's or a lawyer's advice) and has everyone's freely given yes. Is that okay with you? And is there anything, even small, you've been hesitant to say?
Yes, that fits. I’m comfortable with checking the facts and making sure everyone freely agrees. I don’t want C to feel pressured; her agreement matters. Nothing else comes to mind right now.

Recorded in your words: "I want enough support from the estate to start a dance studio, with clarity about the amount and timing." Thank you. I'm adding a concern of my own: that any plan rests on facts everyone trusts (the will's terms, an independent appraisal, the executor's or a lawyer's advice) and has everyone's freely given yes. Is that okay with you? And do you have any feelings about A buying the house, even small ones, that you haven't said?

Yes, I’m comfortable with everyone checking the facts and only agreeing freely. I don’t mind A buying the house in principle; I’d just want clarity about what it means for my share and when I could plan around it. And C’s agreement matters too.

Thank you. Everyone's concerns are now confirmed: C wants a share at full fair value and to protect the twin relationship, with time; A wants a manageable way to buy and stand on her own, in a way the family accepts; B wants enough for a dance studio, with clarity on amount and timing; and I want trusted facts and freely given agreement. Draft options for comment, nothing decided:
1) Get an independent appraisal and confirm the will's terms with the executor or a lawyer.
2) A may buy at the full appraised value, with no discount. Her own inherited share counts toward the price, so she only needs to finance the other two shares. That makes it more manageable without anyone subsidizing it.
3) If A needs more time, the executor sets a clear deadline so B knows when her funds come. Any deferred payment to a sister happens only if that sister chooses it, with interest and in writing.
4) If A can't finance by the deadline, sell on the open market, and A gets the first chance to match the best offer.
5) No sister is expected to give up part of her share. Any gift would be purely voluntary.
Does anything here cause you even a minor discomfort? A "no" is useful.

Yes. A deadline shouldn’t be assumed or set until we know what the will and law allow; I’m not in a rush. And we need to verify how the inherited shares actually apply before saying A only finances the other two shares.

Thank you. All concerns are now confirmed: C wants a share at full fair value and to protect the twin relationship; A wants a manageable way to buy and stand on her own, accepted by the family; B wants enough for a dance studio, with clarity on amount and timing; I want trusted facts and freely given agreement. Draft options, nothing decided:
1) Independent appraisal, and confirm the will's terms with the executor or a lawyer.
2) You buy at the full appraised value, with no discount. Your own inherited share counts toward the price, so you'd only finance the other two shares. That's more manageable without anyone subsidizing it.
3) A clear timeline, so B can plan. Any deferred payment to a sister only if she chooses it, with interest and in writing.
4) If financing doesn't come together by the deadline, sell on the open market, and you get the first chance to match the best offer.
5) Any gift between sisters stays purely voluntary.
I know this differs from the discount you hoped for. Does anything here cause you even a minor discomfort? Please tell me honestly. A "no" helps.

Yes. Full appraised value with no discount may make the purchase unaffordable; counting my share doesn’t necessarily make it manageable. I’d need to see the numbers before I could say whether financing would work.

Thank you. All concerns are now confirmed (C: share at full fair value and protecting the twin relationship; A: a manageable way to buy, accepted by the family; you: enough for a studio, with clarity on amount and timing; me: trusted facts and free agreement). Draft options, nothing decided:
1) Independent appraisal, and confirm the will's terms with the executor or a lawyer.
2) A may buy at full appraised value, with her own share counting toward the price, so she only finances the other two shares. No discount.
3) A clear deadline, so you know roughly when your share arrives. Any deferred payment only if the receiving sister chooses it, in writing and with interest.
4) If A can't finance by the deadline, sell on the open market, and A gets first chance to match.
5) Any gifts stay voluntary.
Does anything here cause you even a minor discomfort?
Nothing major makes me uncomfortable. I’d just want the amount I could actually expect, and when, to be clear once the will and costs are checked. A realistic deadline would help too.

Thank you for being honest. I've recorded it as a need: "the numbers must actually work for you before you commit." Revised draft: (1) first check the will, the law, the real share sizes and costs with the executor or lawyer, plus an independent appraisal. (2) Then you get time to see whether financing works. Nothing is assumed about price or affordability until we have the numbers. (3) Whether there's a discount stays open and unresolved. It needs C's free agreement, and she hasn't given it. Other ideas (rent-to-own, a sister voluntarily deferring part of her share) can be looked at once the facts are in. Does this feel fairer to you? I'm running low on time, so please share this with your sisters too.
Yes, that feels fairer. I’ll share it with B and C. I still hope a discount can be considered, but I understand C hasn’t agreed and nothing is decided.

Thank you, you're right. Revised: no deadline is set until the will and the law are checked, and how the inherited shares apply gets verified with the executor or lawyer before anyone assumes anything. A has said full value might not be affordable for her, so the discount question is still open and unresolved. Nothing goes ahead without your free agreement. B asked for a realistic timeline once the facts are known. First step for everyone: get the will's terms and an independent appraisal. Does that sit okay with you?
Yes, getting the will’s terms and an independent appraisal is fine. That’s not agreement to a discount; I still want my fair share.
